transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I start projects and assignments full of ideas, but I just can’t seem to follow through and finish things, and it’s already cost me my first job. It has been incredibly frustrating and discouraging because I know I have the ability, but I just can't seem to get anything across the finish line.
Do you also often feel physically restless or fidgety, have trouble sitting still, or act impulsively without thinking first?

Yes, completely—if I have to sit still, I get this buzzing feeling under my skin and fidget so much that my friends joke I have a motor with no off switch. I also get really impatient waiting my turn and constantly find myself cutting people off or blurting things out before they can even finish their sentences.
Do these restlessness and impulsive behaviors happen in more than one setting, like at work or school and also at home or with friends?

Yes, absolutely, it happens everywhere. At my old job and in college lectures, I was constantly blurting things out in meetings and couldn't sit still, but even at home with my roommates, I can't just relax and watch a show without pacing around or talking over them.
Did these attention and restlessness problems start in childhood or early teens, and have they been present for at least 6 months?

Yes, they definitely started back in childhood—my elementary school report cards always said I daydreamed, forgot homework, and talked out of turn. They've been going on my whole life, but things became really severe and came to a head over the last year when my responsibilities at the startup ramped up.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview confirms a lifelong pattern beginning in childhood of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity across multiple settings, with clear functional impairment (loss of job). Symptoms have persisted for years and worsened under increased demands, fitting ADHD, predominantly inattentive/hyperactive-impulsive presentation coded as F90.0.
